chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-A'ala, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:
Indeed, the poor among the Muslims will be moving about in the gardens of Paradise before their rich ones by forty autumns.

Then he said: I shall set forth for you the likeness of that. The likeness of that is the likeness of two ships that passed by a tax collector. He looked into one of them and saw nothing in it, so he said: Let it go. And he looked into the other, and found it heavily laden, so he said: Detain it.

key_terms.أَغْنِيَائِهِمْ: their rich ones; those possessing worldly wealth
key_terms.احْبِسُوهَا: detain it; hold it back for inspection
key_terms.خَرِيفًا: autumn; here meaning a year in counting time
key_terms.رِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ: the gardens of Paradise; the places of delight in the Hereafter
key_terms.سَفِينَتَيْنِ: two ships; the metaphor used to explain the difference
key_terms.عَاشِرٍ: a tax collector or tithe-taker who inspects goods
key_terms.فُقَرَاءَ: the poor; those without wealth or worldly means

ai.seo_question: Why do poor Muslims enter Paradise before the rich according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the poor among the Muslims will enter and enjoy Paradise before the wealthy by forty years. It illustrates this through the example of two ships before a tax collector: the empty one passes quickly, while the loaded one is detained, signifying that worldly possessions bring added reckoning in the Hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’ala, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The poor Muslims would be strolling in the Gardens of the Paradise before their rich ones do by forty autumns (years)’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> shall strike an example of that for you. But rather, an example of that is an example of two ships passing by a tax collector. So he looks into one of the two but does not see anything in it. So he says, ‘Let it go’. And he looks into the other one, so it is fully laden. So he says, ‘Withhold it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-‘Ala’ from ibn abu Ya’fur from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The poor Muslims will stroll in the gardens of paradise forty years before the wealthy Muslims.

An example of this is the case of two ships arriving at the tax collector’s post. The tax collector searches one of the ships and finds it empty. He withdraws and the ship is free to go. But he finds the other ship fill of goods. He then orders his people to follow the accounting procedure.’”
